Article Title: 'Gen Z, farmers angry; BJP losing UP': Akhilesh says Centre using delimitation to divert attention
Article Text:
Yadav called delimitation the BJP's “biggest political blunder”

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday accused the BJP of using the proposed delimitation exercise to divert attention from public concerns, including unemployment, farmers' distress and the impact of US tariffs."When Gen Z is angry, farmers are angry, traders are angry, America is slapping tariff after tariff on you... Following the agitations of Gen Z and youth demanding jobs and employment, they are bringing delimitation just to divert their attention," he said while speaking to news agency ANI.Speaking in Sambhal, Yadav called delimitation the BJP's “biggest political blunder” and alleged that the party was worried about losing Uttar Pradesh. “When Gen Z is angry, farmers are angry, traders are angry, America is slapping tariff after tariff on you... they are bringing delimitation just to divert their attention,” he said.Yadav said the Samajwadi Party supports women's reservation but questioned the proposed increase in Lok Sabha seats alongside the exercise. He alleged that under the pretext of implementing 33% women's reservation and increasing representation, the government was planning to raise the number of seats by 50%, with constituency boundaries already predetermined.“How can you trust the BJP, which is unable to secure the country's borders, when it is redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha constituencies?” he asked.Taking a swipe at the BJP's political messaging, Yadav said the party's previous narratives had failed and mocked its slogan, “Radhe-Radhe kamal khila de”.Uttar Pradesh is likely to go to the polls in February 2027, following a schedule similar to the 2022 Assembly elections. The Election Commission is expected to begin reviewing poll preparedness soon before undertaking a full-fledged assessment in Decemeber.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of using the proposed delimitation exercise to divert attention from public concerns. Yadav called delimitation the BJP's “biggest political blunder” and alleged that the party was worried about losing Uttar Pradesh. “How can you trust the BJP, which is unable to secure the country's borders,” he asked.

Article Title: CM Shivakumar warns of 'Delhi Chalo' stir if Centre continues to withhold drought aid

To meet Kerala, Telangana CMs over delimitation

NEW DELHI: Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar on Saturday warned of a 'Delhi Chalo' agitation after the Belagavi winter session if the Centre failed to release drought relief funds to the state before the session concludes. He also announced a meeting with the chief ministers of Kerala and Telangana in Delhi on Sunday to discuss the proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies, alleging that the exercise could disadvantage southern states.Addressing a press conference at the Sangama conference hall in Vidhana Soudha, Shivakumar said Karnataka had not received any drought relief from the Centre so far, news agency IANS reported."We have discussed this issue in the Cabinet and will launch all forms of protest. If the Centre does not release compensation before the conclusion of the Belagavi session, we will launch a Delhi Chalo agitation after the session," he said.Asked whether the state would approach the Supreme Court if the Centre failed to release the funds, Shivakumar said the government would move the court. He added that it had also sought an appointment with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss the matter through an all-party delegation.On his Delhi visit, Shivakumar said he would leave Bengaluru on Saturday night and meet the chief ministers of Kerala and Telangana on Sunday to discuss the Centre's proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies."We will discuss the injustice being done to our state, the likely increase in the number of seats in northern states, and the implications for southern states. We have only the information available through media reports about the decision taken by the Union Cabinet. We will fight to protect our interests," he said.Accusing the BJP of pursuing delimitation to suit its political interests, Shivakumar said southern states could become minorities in terms of parliamentary representation despite their contribution to the country's development."We support women's reservation, but oppose delimitation. The BJP is doing this according to its convenience. We will fight to protect our sovereignty and interests. They cannot suppress our voice," he said.He also questioned why the Centre had not convened an all-party meeting to discuss the proposed exercise
Article Summary: Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar warns of a 'Delhi Chalo' agitation after the Belagavi winter session. He also announced a meeting with the chief ministers of Kerala and Telangana in Delhi on Sunday to discuss the proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies.

Article Title: 'I have endured a lot': Mamata's brother seeks FIR against nephew Abhishek over 'threats'
Article Text:
Family feud escalates: Mamata's brother moves police against Abhishek over threats

NEW DELHI: The younger brother of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee , Swapan Banerjee on Thursday approached the police seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee , alleging intimidation and obstruction to a blood donation camp, news agency PTI reported.Swapan, popularly known as Babun, alleged that a culture of threats and intimidation had taken root during the TMC's 15-year rule in the state and continued even after the BJP came to power in May this year. He claimed to have witnessed such incidents since 2024."Many things happened during the TMC regime. This has been going on since 2024 and continues even today. There have been instances of obstruction of government work, forcible takeover of clubs and intimidation. How much can I say? I have endured a lot," he told reporters after approaching the Kalighat police station.The immediate trigger for the complaint was allegedly the obstruction of a blood donation camp. However, details of the incident and the specific allegations levelled against the TMC national general secretary were not immediately available.The complaint marks another escalation in the long-standing estrangement between Babun and Mamata Banerjee.The former chief minister had publicly distanced herself from her younger brother at one point, even declaring that she had severed ties with him.The family discord has taken on a political dimension following the BJP's victory in the assembly elections, which ended the TMC's uninterrupted 15-year rule in West Bengal.Since the change of government, Babun has increasingly been seen getting closer to the BJP leadership and has repeatedly praised chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.He recently invited Suvendu Adhikari to inaugurate a community Durga Puja in his neighbourhood and was also seen touching the chief minister's feet as a mark of respect during the event.His repeated public expressions of admiration for Suvendu have fuelled speculation about his political leanings and a possible shift towards the BJP.However, Babun has not made any formal announcement about joining the BJP.
Article Summary: Swapan Banerjee has approached the police seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and TMC MP Abhishek. The complaint marks another escalation in the long-standing estrangement between Babun and Mamata. The former chief minister had publicly distanced herself from her younger brother at one point, even declaring that she had severed ties with him.

Article Title: 'Hail Lord Murugan': PM Modi's post amid SC verdict on Deepam row
Article Text:
The Supreme Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government for not complying with its order

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday posted the Tamil phrase "Vetrivel Muruganukku Arogara", which translates to "Victory to Lord Murugan".PM Modi also wrote the phrase in both English and Hindi scripts.Although the Prime Minister did not provide any further details, the post came hours after the Supreme Court delivered its order in the matter concerning Madurai's Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Murugan.Earlier in the day, the Supreme Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government for defying its order allowing a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai.The lamp was lit at its customary spot at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple instead. The state government cited law and order concerns for not complying with the court's directive.Earlier in the day, while hearing a contempt petition against the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government, the Supreme Court observed that its November 20 order directing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam atop Thiruparankundram Hill on November 24, the day of the festival, had been violated.It ordered that the lamp be lit again on Saturday.After hearing the petitioners and submissions on behalf of the Madurai district collector, the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department and the police commissioner, the top court issued a series of interim directions.The court held that the Tamil Nadu government and the Thiruparankundram Temple's Board of Trustees had collectively failed to comply with its directions. It also found grounds to initiate contempt proceedings against the district collector, HR&CE officials, the police commissioner and members of the temple's board, directing them to appear before it on December 15.The Supreme Court also observed that the temple's administration was not being properly managed by the Board of Trustees. It appointed retired Madras high court judges Justice Vaidyanathan and Justice Parthiban to oversee the temple's administration and directed them to assume charge immediately, either on the same day or the following day.In another significant direction, the court ordered that the entire Thiruparankundram Hill be brought under the security cover of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). Directions were reportedly issued to CISF officials in Chennai to implement the order.The court further directed that the Karthigai Deepam be lit atop the hill the following day, noting that the entire month fell within the Tamil month of Karthigai. It also ordered that compliance be reported to the court.In its interim order, the Supreme Court took a strong view of the conduct of government officials, observing that they had failed to discharge their duties and acted in violation of the law.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday posted the Tamil phrase "Vetrivel Muruganukku Arogara", which translates to "Victory to Lord MurUGan" PM Modi also wrote the phrase in both English and Hindi scripts. The post came hours after the Supreme Court delivered its order in the matter concerning Madurai's Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple. The Supreme Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government for defying its order.

Article Title: Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das
Article Text:
Senior counsel Akhil Sibal, representing Das, told Justice Amit Mahajan that his client had never been told of a lookout circular against him. He asked for a copy of the document along with an explanation of its “purpose”.

Can’t give LOC copy as Das yet to respond to Nov 23 notice: Government

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Centre informed Delhi high court on Thursday that a lookout circular had been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das at the request of Mumbai police early on Nov 23, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport barred him from flying to London. Besides Das, lookout circulars have been issued against CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka over CJP’s protest at Dadar on October 2.Centre’s counsel said Das was free to challenge the circular in the appropriate court, reiterating that the CJP functionary also faces scrutiny for “multiple discrepancies” in his passport that could affect his citizenship.Das’s lawyers had filed a petition seeking clarity on why he was issued a notice about alleged discrepancies in his passport on the day he was to fly to UK.“The LOC is clearly an afterthought,” Das said in a statement later, asking why declared fugitives such as Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi had been allowed to leave the country while activists like him were being stopped.Senior counsel Akhil Sibal, representing Das, told Justice Amit Mahajan that his client had never been told of a lookout circular against him. He asked for a copy of the document along with an explanation of its “purpose”.The counsel said enforcement agencies were awaiting the outcome of an inquiry that started in Puducherry to verify Das’s place of birth, address and parentage, pointing out that the passport column meant to have details of his father had been left blank.He said that, assuming passport authorities find Das’s explanation inadequate, he could be “left stranded in no-man’s land”.Additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma and standing counsel Ashish Dixit said a copy of the lookout circular could not be immediately given to Das because he was yet to respond to the show-cause notice issued on Nov 23.That notice, Sharma said, states that inputs were received indicating Das’s place of birth was incorrect and that his passport had been obtained by suppressing facts. “It requires clarification and supporting documents, failing which the passport may be suspended or impounded,” he said.The ASG also told the court that Madras HC issued notice on a plea seeking an inquiry into Das’s antecedents on Oct 30.Sibal countered that a pending show-cause notice over discrepancies could not translate into a travel ban. “There is no revocation, suspension, impounding of the passport. The show-cause notice doesn’t mean necessarily there will be harsh consequences… he will respond to the notice in due course,” he said, arguing that travel was a fundamental right.
Article Summary: Centre informed Delhi high court on Thursday that a lookout circular had been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das. The circular was issued at the request of Mumbai police early on Nov 23, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport barred him from flying to London. Das’s lawyers had filed a petition seeking clarity on why he was issued a notice about alleged discrepancies in his passport.

Article Title: Opposition mood despondent as NCP (SP), DMK change stand
Article Text:
Vowing to 'expose' BJP, AICC general secretary K C Venugopal said, 'Modi and Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India'

NEW DELHI: The opposition Friday was staring at possible passage of the delimitation bill, after DMK and NCP (SP), which were critical to its defeat in April, signalled willingness to back the legislation. Congress said BJP wants to “change the Constitution” through delimitation after the ruling party failed to achieve it with the “400 paar” election, alleging the redrawing of LS seats would be done by “compromised” CEC Gyanesh Kumar, who has been “exposed” for manipulating electoral rolls.Vowing to “expose” BJP, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal said, “Modi and Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this episode.” But the mood in the opposition was despondent as its persisting confidence about unity in the anti-bill ranks dissipated with statements from M K Stalin and NCP (SP) leaders.There was regret within that the Congress’s decision to abruptly dump a staunch ally, the DMK, in favour of TVK to form govt in TN had angered the Dravidian party into drifting towards BJP. The attacks from Congress leaders on DMK on Friday reflected the anger at the former ally, even as TN Congress members were peppered with queries about whether they regretted leaving the DMK alliance.Ahead of the special sitting of Parliament, BJD Friday said party president Naveen Patnaik will take the final call on delimitation and the women’s reservation bills, with Odisha’s interests guiding the party’s stand, reports Ashok Pradhan. “Our decision will be guided by Odisha’s interests. Once we get a clear idea about the agenda and details of the bills, we will take an appropriate decision as per our party chief’s direction,” said Manas Mangaraj, head of BJD parliamentary party in Rajya Sabha.BJD has five members in Rajya Sabha but no representation in Lok Sabha.

DMK and NCP (SP), which were critical to its defeat in April, signalled willingness to back the legislation. BJD said party president Naveen Patnaik will take the final call on delimitation and women’s reservation bills.

Article Title: Supreme Court junks plea seeking its intervention to remove Italian politician’s ‘vote chor’ remark on socials
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said the petitioner may file a representation to the Centre on his plea for framing regulations on speeches made by foreigners on Indian soil.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a plea seeking its intervention in the controversy of Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck shouting the slogan “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod” at Hyderabad during “Bharat Summit” and for the removal of his views from social media.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said the petitioner may file a representation to the Centre on his plea for framing regulations on speeches made by foreigners on Indian soil. “You are free to make representations. Who is stopping you!” “You can file a complaint. Why Article 32 petition?” SC said. The petitioner said Filibeck interfered in India’s domestic political affairs.Filibeck, secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists, triggered a controversy with the purported slogan and praise for Rahul Gandhi for his campaign for clean and transparent electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck shouted the slogan “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod’ at Hyderabad during “Bharat Summit” and for the removal of his views from social media. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh said the petitioner may file a representation to the Centre on his plea.

Article Title: Sonia Gandhi was not an Indian citizen in 1980 but name on voter list: Delhi Police tells court
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police on Saturday told a Delhi court that Sonia Gandhi was not an Indian citizen in 1980, despite her name appearing on the electoral roll that year, news agency ANI reported.The submission came after the Rouse Avenue Court sought an action taken report (ATR) from the Station House Officer (SHO) of IP Estate Police Station on a complaint alleging that the Congress leader's name was included in the voter list nearly three years before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983.The complaint questions how Sonia Gandhi's name could have featured in the electoral roll in 1980, when she was not an Indian citizen. It seeks a police investigation into what it describes as a possible case of forgery.On Saturday, the Delhi Police told the court that Sonia Gandhi acquired Indian citizenship only in 1983. It added that the facts had been verified by the district magistrate and the ministry of home affairs.The court granted the Delhi Police more time to complete its inquiry and scheduled the next hearing for December 14. It also summoned the SHO of Tughlak Road Police Station.
Article Summary: Delhi Police tells court Sonia Gandhi was not an Indian citizen in 1980. Her name appeared on the electoral roll that year, despite her not being a citizen. Delhi Police says Sonia Gandhi acquired Indian citizenship only in 1983. The court granted the Delhi Police more time to complete its inquiry.

Article Title: 'Shift stance, set aside politics': Kiren Rijiju urges Congress to back Delimitation Bill
Article Text:
Rijiju accused the opposition party of not believing in democratic processes.

'Congress has never believed in democracy': Rijiju

NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday urged the Congress to set aside political differences and support the Delimitation Bill, saying the concerns raised by various states and communities had been addressed.Appealing to the Congress to reconsider its opposition, Rijiju said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made a proposal that took into account the interests of every state while seeking to ensure 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies."I believe that following the Prime Minister's appeal, the Congress party must also shift its long-held stance and outdated mindset. I urge the Congress party, as well as those few others who are opposing this bill at the behest of the Congress, to set aside politics and join hands in Parliament to work towards women's empowerment and ensure the passage of this bill," he said.Rijiju said the proposed legislation would not only provide 33% reservation for women but also increase the number of elected representatives in Parliament and state assemblies.He maintained that the proposal addressed the interests of all states and communities, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and questioned why the Congress was opposing a measure aimed at women's empowerment.Responding to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's remarks on the bill, Rijiju accused the opposition party of not believing in democratic processes."The Congress party has never believed in democracy. We are seeking support for the sake of the democratic system itself. Otherwise, why would we even bring a bill forward? We could have just passed it," he said.He stressed that the government was seeking the bill's passage through a democratic process and appealed to the Congress not to turn the issue into a political confrontation.On Kharge's remarks, he further suggested that Rahul Gandhi might have influenced the Congress president's position, while adding that he could not say so with certainty."I cannot say for sure, but perhaps Rahul Gandhi ji pressured him; I really don't know. This is not the time for politics. What objection could there possibly be to empowering women?" Rijiju said.Centre is set to introduce the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeking to implement one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state and Union territory legislative assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise.The proposed legislation differs from the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, defeated in the Lok Sabha in April, mainly in its approach to delimitation, the allocation of seats among states and the census data to be used for redrawing constituencies.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju urges Congress to set aside political differences and support the Delimitation Bill. PM Narendra Modi had made a proposal that took into account the interests of every state, he said. He questioned why the Congress was opposing a measure aimed at women's empowerment.

Article Title: 'All MPs should support it rising above party lines': Suvendu Adhikari on delimitation Bill
Article Text:
Suvendu Adhikari calls on MPs to back the delimitation-linked women's reservation bills beyond party lines

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday urged all MPs to support the proposed women's reservation and delimitation-linked bills in Parliament, saying they should rise above party lines. He expressed confidence that the legislation would be passed with a two-thirds majority during the special session beginning November 30."The bills will be passed with a two-thirds majority," news agency PTI quoted Adhikari as saying."Everyone (MPs) should support the bills rising above party lines. Those who want the empowerment of our mothers and sisters will vote in favour of the bills,” he added.The Centre has convened a four-day special sitting of Parliament from November 30. It plans to introduce three bills, including a Constitution amendment, to implement 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies before the 2029 parliamentary elections. The proposed legislation also provides for a 50% increase in seats for each state.The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850. This would include up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories.It also proposes increasing the maximum strength of a state assembly from 500 to 650.The legislation links the implementation of women's reservation with the proposed expansion of legislatures and delimitation.Ahead of the special sitting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said his government would remove every obstacle to implementing 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.In a video message posted on X, PM Modi said the government remained committed to fulfilling its promise to the country's 'Nari Shakti'."Our resolve to empower 'Nari Shakti' remains unshaken. I want to assure every woman in the country that we will definitely eliminate and remove every obstacle that comes in the way of women's reservation," he said.The prime minister said those opposing the legislation would not be able to stop women's increased participation in Parliament and state assemblies."The parties opposing women's reservation will never be able to stop the country's 'Nari Shakti' from increasing their participation in Parliament and the state assemblies. It is just a matter of time," he said.PM Modi added that the supporters of the Bill were determined to see it through, saying, "our courage is unbreakable, and our resolve is steadfast".
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari calls on MPs to back the delimitation-linked women's reservation bills beyond party lines. Centre has convened a four-day special sitting of Parliament from November 30. It plans to introduce three bills, including a Constitution amendment, to implement 33% reservation for women.

Article Title: 'Cares about LS constituencies' borders, not country's': Akhilesh takes swipe at BJP over delimitation
Article Text:
Akhilesh takes swipe at BJP over delimitation

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday stepped up his criticism of BJP over the proposed delimitation exercise, accusing the ruling party of prioritising electoral interests over national concerns.In a post on X, Akhilesh questioned the Centre's focus on redrawing parliamentary constituency boundaries, contrasting it with what he described as its lack of concern for the country's international borders."For the BJP, elections are everything, not the country. That is why it is concerned about the boundaries of Lok Sabha constituencies, but not the country's borders," Akhilesh said.His latest remarks came a day after he described the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation as the BJP's “biggest political mistake”.“Delimitation will prove to be the biggest political mistake made by the BJP,” Akhilesh said in a post on X on Friday.His criticism comes amid preparations for a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3, which the government has convened to transact “essential” business. The proposed legislative package, cleared by the Union Cabinet, is expected to be taken up during the sitting.The Bills seek to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from its existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 and raise the maximum strength of state legislative assemblies to 650.Uttar Pradesh, the country's most populous state, could see its Assembly strength increase from 403 to 650 seats.The proposals also seek to facilitate the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections. The revised seat allocations and constituency boundaries are proposed to remain in force until 2051.Under the proposed framework, the Centre plans to delink the implementation of women's reservation from the 2026 Census and use the 2011 Census figures for delimitation and constituency readjustment, while retaining the 1971 Census as the basis for determining the proportion of seats allocated to different states.The legislative package comprises two Constitution Amendment Bills and one Union Territories Amendment Bill. The Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill proposes changes relating to the state-wise allocation of seats, retaining the 1971 Census as the basis for determining the proportion of seats allotted to different states.
Article Summary: Akhilesh questions Centre's focus on redrawing parliamentary constituency boundaries. He accuses ruling party of prioritising electoral interests over national concerns. His criticism comes amid preparations for a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3. The proposed legislative package is expected to be taken up during the sitting.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Article Title: DMK 'ready' to support BJP's delimitation bill if Tamil Nadu's representation remains unchanged
Article Text:
(PTI File Photo) Union Home minister Amit Shah with MK Stalin during the meeting of 'Southern Zonal Council' in Thiruvananthapuram.

Poll Vote & Share your view Are you in favor of freezing the Lok Sabha seats at 543? Yes, it ensures stability. No, more representation is needed. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





CHENNAI: DMK is ready to support the BJP-led Union govt’s proposed delimitation bill if it maintains Tamil Nadu ’s existing percentage of representation and includes a provision for a 25-year freeze, party sources told TOI.It is reliably learned that DMK leadership placed these two demands before the BJP when the latter recently reached out to the Dravidian party.Asked if the party would support a 50% increase in the number of seats across all states from the current strength, a senior DMK leader said, “Yes, with provision built in the bill for a 25-year freeze and maintaining existing representation from all states. Had we not opposed the bill in the past, we could have lost this proposition. If BJP is ready to incorporate these two demands, we have nothing to lose but to gain more in future. ”DMK had opposed delimitation because Tamil Nadu’s representation could be reduced if the 2027 census was used as the basis for the exercise, sources said.“If the new draft bill ensures Tamil Nadu will continue to have the same percentage representation and next delimitation based on the latest census will be carried out only after 25 years, not 100 years as suggested by few, it is a fair deal.It will be beneficial for both DMK as well as Tamil Nadu,” a source said.Asked whether the BJP had recently reached out to DMK, the source said, “Yes, they did and we have given them the demands.”DMK has 22 MPs in Lok Sabha and 8 MPs in Rajya Sabha. The party has maintained that it is not opposed to delimitation but wants the process to be fair to all sides. In August, DMK backed a resolution of the TVK govt in the assembly urging the Union govt to freeze the current strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 seats.DMK chief and former Tamil Nadu chief minister, MK Stalin, in a post on X, said, “If the number of parliamentary constituencies is increased, under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu’s share fall below its current 7.18%! The existing proportion of parliamentary representation among States, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years!”“The DMK remains firm on both these positions today and will continue to do so. The speculation being spread in the media and the grumbling of backstabbers will not shake our position in any way. The DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests,” he added.Meanwhile, CPM state secretary Shanmugam expressed concern over reports that the Union govt had “reached an understanding” with the DMK on the delimitation bill. “On behalf of the CPM, we urge the DMK to remain steadfast in its commitment to protecting the interests of Tamil Nadu and the southern states,” he posted on X.Shanmugam urged the DMK leadership to clarify its stance on delimitation without leaving room for speculation.
Article Summary: DMK has 22 MPs in Lok Sabha and 8 MPs in Rajya Sabha. The party has maintained that it is not opposed to delimitation but wants the process to be fair to all sides. In August, DMK backed a resolution urging the Union govt to freeze the current strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 seats.

Article Title: Fake SIM supply racket busted, 7 held
Article Text:
DSP (Cyber) Kailash Prasad Mahato said four of the seven accused were residents of Birbhum in West Bengal, while the rest were of Dumka district in Jharkhand

Dumka:





Seven miscreants have been arrested from Palajori police station area in Deoghar late Friday on charges of supplying fraudulently procured SIM cards to cyber criminals in several states, police said on Saturday.DSP (Cyber) Kailash Prasad Mahato said, “Acting on the orders of Deoghar SP Praveen Pushkar, seven persons were arrested and eight mobile phones along with 32 SIM cards were seized.”The accused have been identified as Hasib Momin, Sarjahan Momin, Kamal Momin, and Rajababu Momin, all residents of Birbhum district in West Bengal, and Azrul Ansari, Nizam Ansari, and Sarfuddin Ansari, residents of Masalia police station area in Dumka district Technical analysis of the seized mobile numbers and IMEI details revealed links to cyber fraud cases lodged across states. The racket allegedly used the identities of West Bengal residents to procure SIM cards, which were then supplied to cyber criminals for use in online fraud.“Further investigation is under way to ascertain the racket’s network and its links with cyber criminals,” he added.
Article Summary: Four of the seven accused were residents of Birbhum in West Bengal, while the rest were of Dumka district in Jharkhand. The racket allegedly used the identities of West Bengal residents to procure SIM cards, which were then supplied to cyber criminals for use in online fraud.

Article Title: No Region Will Face Injustice Due To Delimitation: Ramchander Rao
Article Text: Hyderabad: BJP state president N Ramchander Rao said no region will face injustice due to the delimitation of the constituencies. He said the Centre is moving forward with the idea of proportionately increasing the current number of seats by 50 percent. Because of this, assembly seats in Telangana are likely to increase to over 170, and Parliament seats from 17 to 25.“According to Article 81 of the Constitution, seat allocation must be based on population under the ‘One Person - One Vote - One Value’ principle. To ensure that Southern and North-Eastern states do not suffer any loss from this,“ the BJP president said at a press conference on Saturday.He further explained that increasing seats in proportion to population growth is inevitable. “In 1971, when the country’s population was 56 crores, there were 543 Parliament seats. Today, the population has tripled to 140–145 crores. Since the census did not take place in 2021, it was essential to increase seats based on the 2011 census. This will significantly boost the representation of SC, ST, BC communities, and women in legislative bodies,” he said.Ramchander Rao said currently, there was a massive disparity in the number of voters between constituencies.“For example, while the Malkajgiri Parliamentary constituency has 40 lakh voters, Secunderabad has 11 lakh voters. Similarly, among Assembly seats, Serilingampally has 7.5 lakh voters, whereas Amberpet has only 2.5 lakh voters. We are undertaking the delimitation process specifically to rectify these inequalities and distribute the number of voters equally across all constituencies,“ he said.Criticising Congress stand on the bill, Ramchander Rao alleged that in the past, Rajiv Gandhi merely created hype in the name of women’s reservations without implementing it and during the UPA regime, their own allies blocked the bill.He said while pretending externally to support women’s reservations, the Congress party is internally conspiring to obstruct delimitation and the reservation bill. Rahul Gandhi and Revanth Reddy, with their baseless statements, are preventing political justice from reaching SCs, STs, BCs, and women,He urged all parties should support the NDA govt on women’s reservation and delimitation Bills.ends/
Article Summary: BJP state president N Ramchander Rao said no region will face injustice. He said the Centre is moving forward with the idea of proportionately increasing the current number of seats by 50 percent. Because of this, assembly seats in Telangana are likely to increase to over 170, and Parliament seats from 17 to 25.

Article Title: Beed cop flees with bribe money, car after spotting ACB trap
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A police head constable allegedly fled with Rs 5,000 in bribe money in his private car after spotting an Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) team laying a trap at Gevrai police station in Beed district late Thursday.According to ACB officials, he asked the complainant and panch witnesses to get out of the car before speeding away. The incident has caused embarrassment to the ACB, particularly because the accused allegedly escaped with the bribe amount despite the presence of its team.“The accused, Pandurang Uttam Darade, a head constable posted at Gevrai police station, has not yet been arrested. The ACB has launched a search for him and registered an offence against him under the relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act,” said Superintendent of Police (ACB) Madhuri Kedar Kangane.According to the ACB, the 26-year-old complainant, who is a farmer, submitted a written complaint on Nov 26, alleging that Darade had demanded Rs 7,000 to facilitate the return of his stolen car. During verification on the same day, the ACB found that the head constable had initially demanded Rs 7,000 and later agreed to accept Rs 5,000 after negotiations.The ACB team then laid a trap at Gevrai police station. As planned, Darade accepted Rs 5,000 from the complainant inside his private car, in the presence of panch witnesses.However, as the trap team moved in, Darade apparently sensed its presence. He allegedly asked the complainant and the panch witnesses to get out of the car and immediately fled from the spot with the vehicle and the bribe money.The ACB team, led by deputy superintendent Sopan Chittampalle, is conducting further investigation and efforts are underway to trace the absconding head constable. The process of searching his residence is also underway.An offence under Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and Section 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, has been registered.
Article Summary: A police head constable allegedly fled with Rs 5,000 in bribe money in his private car after spotting an Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) team laying a trap at Gevrai police station. The incident has caused embarrassment to the ACB, particularly because the accused allegedly escaped with the bribe amount despite the presence of its team.

Article Title: Solapur DCC Bank polls: BJP-backed panel wins 8 of 9 contested seats, takes tally to 18

Celebrations outside counting centre by supporters over Solapur DCC bank win

Kolhapur





: A BJP-backed panel on Friday won eight of the nine seats in the Solapur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank that went to the polls, after 10 seats were earlier won unopposed.In the 19-member board of directors, the BJP-backed panel has won a total of 18 seats. Article Title: 3 sanitary workers suffocate to death in Maharashtra's Sangli septic tank; negligence, say cops
Article Text:
Three conservancy workers suffocated to death while attempting to clean a septic tank in Sangli.





KOLHAPUR: Three conservancy workers suffocated to death within 15 minutes of entering a septic tank at Shirdhon village in Sangli’s Kavathe Mahankal taluka on Friday, police said.The owner of a private hotel and lawn along Pandharpur road had hired the workers to clean the tank. Five workers arrived in the morning to carry out the task. Yashwant Biru Shelake (50) entered the tank first. When he did not respond to calls, Akash Anil Bagade (23) went down to rescue him, police said. After neither responded, Tushar Balasaheb Koshti (25) entered the tank.All three were brought out and taken to Kavathe Mahankal’s sub-district hospital, where doctors declared them dead on arrival, police said.“Preliminary investigation indicated negligence in the septic tank deaths. No safety gear was used and the workers entered the tank, around eight-foot-deep, using a ladder without checking oxygen levels,” Kavathe Mahankal police station in-charge Pravinkumar Kamble said.
Article Summary: The owner of a private hotel and lawn along Pandharpur road had hired the workers to clean the tank. Five workers arrived in the morning to carry out the task. No safety gear was used and the workers entered the tank, around eight- foot-deep, using a ladder without checking oxygen levels.

Article Title: Increasing MP count to 815 would give no opportunity to speak, says ex-CM Chavan
Article Text:
Former Maharashtra chief minister Prithviraj Chavan

Kolhapur:





Former MP and ex-CM of Maharashtra Prithviraj Chavan said on Friday that raising the number of MPs from 543 to 815 through the proposed delimitation bill will not give any member a chance to speak.“It will be similar to general body meetings of cooperative sugar mills. Therefore, I personally and my party oppose raising the number of MPs to 815,” Chavan said while speaking in Karad on the proposed delimitation bill.Chavan said that his party was not opposed to delimitation but wants relative representation of states in Lok Sabha to remain on the basis of the 1971 census. “If the 1971 freeze formula is changed and 2011 census is used, it will be an injustice to southern states. The Lok Sabha seats were frozen at 543 in 1976, that too twice, the latest one by Atal Bihari Vajpayee ’s govt,” said Chavan.The ex-CM also claimed that Centre was misleading people by stating that delimitation was necessary to introduce women’s reservation. “There is no connection between the two. The women’s reservation bill was passed unanimously when it was tabled in 2023. If you want to implement it, start it from coming state elections; why wait for delimitation and census to happen?” added Chavan.
Article Summary: Prithviraj Chavan says raising the number of MPs from 543 to 815 will not give any member a chance to speak. Chavan said that his party was not opposed to delimitation but wants relative representation of states in Lok Sabha to remain on the basis of the 1971 census.

Article Title: DMK backs Centre's delimitation bill, says Tamil Nadu's representation will rise from 7.18% to 7.21%
Article Text:
(PTI File Photo) PM Narendra Modi and DMK chief MK Stalin





CHENNAI: The DMK , which has 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha, has decided to support the revised delimitation bill, claiming that its three-year campaign has secured safeguards to protect Tamil Nadu 's share of parliamentary representation.The decision was taken at a meeting of the party's MPs chaired by DMK president M K Stalin at Anna Arivalayam on Saturday, following a detailed discussion on the bill.DMK deputy secretary A Raja made officially declared the decision. DMK chief Stalin defended the decision as a victory for the party's sustained campaign against delimitation, saying the revised proposal incorporated the two key demands it had put forward through a TN’s Assembly resolution in 2024.The bill provides for a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, which would raise Tamil Nadu's representation from 39 to 51 seats, while marginally increasing its share from 7.18% to 7.21%, deputy secretary and MP A Raja said.The DMK had opposed the earlier bill brought hurriedly in April, arguing that delimitation based on population figures would disproportionately benefit northern states and dilute TN's representation.Stalin said the party had prevented such an outcome by pushing for a practical alternative that ensured an increase in seats without compromising the state's share.The party has not deviated from its stand on fair delimitation, Raja told reporters, hitting back at former ally Congress for accusing the DMK of changing its position. It was the DMK that had proposed the concept of fair delimitation and other parties had subsequently accepted it, he said, describing the criticism as "shameful".The DMK has constituted a team to examine the bill in detail and raise concerns, if any, during parliamentary proceedings, Raja said.Responding to former Union minister P Chidambaram 's concerns that the BJP could target minorities through the bill, Raja said the DMK would not compromise on minority rights and would continue to flag concerns and fight to protect them.MP Dhayanidhi Maran later told reporters that there is going to be no change as the fair delimitation increases the seat by 50% across the country. “The situation will remain the same even after the increase (of seats). No state is going to lose or gain disproportionately from this.”Defending the party’s decision, he said, “Our demand has been accepted. We want the status quo to prevail. Either there should be no delimitation, or if delimitation is carried out, our rights must be protected. The number of seats for southern states should not be reduced, and northern states should not get disproportionately more seats. Today, Uttar Pradesh is also getting a 50 per cent increase, Bihar is also getting a 50 per cent increase, and Tamil Nadu is also getting a 50 per cent increase. This is the status quo. There is no change. We are ensuring that our rights are protected for the next 25 years, apart from the implementation of women's reservation.”
Article Summary: The decision was taken at a meeting of the party's MPs chaired by DMK president M K Stalin. The bill provides for a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states. It would raise Tamil Nadu's representation from 39 to 51 seats, while marginally increasing its share from 7.18% to 7.21%.

Article Title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh remanded in 14-day judicial custody, lodged in Cuddalore Central Prison
Article Text:
Kallakurichi Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA C Arul Vignesh was arrested for allegedly harassing a woman IAS officer.





KALLAKURICHI: Kallakurichi Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh, who was arrested in connection with a case of allegedly harassing a woman IAS officer, has been remanded to 14 days of judicial custody and lodged in the Cuddalore Central Prison early on Saturday.Tirupur superintendent of police Srishti Singh, who was appointed as the investigating officer in the case, had camped in Kallakurichi over the past three days to conduct inquiries.Following the probe, police arrested Vignesh from his residence in Kallakurichi on Friday evening.After the arrest, Singh questioned the legislator for over five hours at the Kallakurichi government guest house in Thiyagadurgam.He was subsequently taken to the Kallakurichi Govt Medical College Hospital for a routine medical examination before being produced before a judicial magistrate.The magistrate remanded Vignesh to judicial custody for 14 days. Following the court order, police escorted him under tight security to Cuddalore, where he was lodged in the Cuddalore Central Prison at 4.05am on Saturday.A heavy police force was deployed around the central prison complex to avoid any untoward incident.
Article Summary: Kallakurichi Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh was arrested in connection with a case of allegedly harassing a woman IAS officer. He has been remanded to 14 days of judicial custody and lodged in the Cuddalore Central Prison.

Article Title: Woman, daughter drown as car plunges into PAP canal near Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A 70-year-old woman and her 43-year-old daughter drowned after the car they were travelling in plunged into the Parambikulam-Aliyar Project (PAP) canal near Sulthanpet in Coimbatore district on Friday afternoon.The deceased were identified as N Saraswathi and her daughter Mani, both residents of Periyapatti near Udumalpet in Tirupur district. They were travelling to a relative’s farm at Periyakammalapatti near Sulthanpet in Coimbatore, in their car driven by acting driver Raghunath, 34, a resident of Udumalpet.When the vehicle reached Periyakammalapatti, the driver reportedly lost control, causing the car to veer off the road and plunge into the canal.Raghunath managed to escape from the vehicle, but Saraswathi and Mani were trapped inside.Passers-by alerted the Sulthanpet police and the Sulur Fire and Rescue Services personnel, who rushed to the spot. After a brief struggle, they retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Palladam Govt Hospital for postmortem. Sulthanpet police have registered a case.
Article Summary: The deceased were identified as N Saraswathi and her daughter Mani. They were travelling to a relative’s farm at Periyakammalapatti near Sulthanpet in Coimbatore. The driver reportedly lost control, causing the car to veer off the road.

Article Title: Coimbatore corporation school teacher arrested for sexually harassing girl students
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: A 45-year-old mathematics teacher working at a corporation school in Coimbatore was arrested under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act for allegedly sexually harassing girl students.According to police, the accused, Senthilkumar, had allegedly subjected some girl students to sexual harassment. Article Title: Man abducted, assaulted by gang in Coimbatore
Article Text:

COIMBATORE: A man was abducted and assaulted by a four-member gang here on Wednesday demanding information about an advocate.The complainant, P Balsankar, 34, of Maruthamalai Gounder Layout in Ganapathy , was acquainted with one of the accused, Vijay Anand.According to the complaint, Vijay Anand, Raja, Prabhu and Deepak forcibly took Balsankar in a car towards Thudiyalur around 1.30pm on Thursday. Article Title: Tirupur farmers hold protest seeking full waiver of cooperative crop loans
Article Text: TIRUPUR: More than 100 farmers held a protest in front of the Tirupur district collectorate condemning state govt for not fully waiving cooperative crop loans. They urged govt to implement the complete waiver promised during the elections.The agitation was led by N Ramesh, Tirupur city and district secretary of Tamil Nadu Farmers Protection Association. He said chief minister C Joseph Vijay, during the poll campaign, had assured that cooperative crop loans would be waived fully for farmers owning under five acres and by 50% for those owning above five acres, without conditions, calling it a “guarantee.”Ramesh said Tamil Nadu’s farmers had availed cooperative crop loans of around Rs 20,000 crore, but govt initially announced only Rs 2,000 crore in the first phase, triggering widespread disappointment. Following sustained protests by farmers and farm bodies, the relief ceiling for beneficiaries was raised, with the amount increased to Rs 35,000 from an earlier Rs 5,000 for farmers with loans above Rs 1 lakh, he said.He added that more than 50 farmers’ organisations had formed a federation and held continuous sit-in protests. Later, during talks in Chennai, it was announced that Rs 75,000 would be provided to all, he said.However, farmers alleged that multiple conditions remained and those who took crop loans during 2022, 2023, 2024 and in Jan-April 2025 were left out. With monsoon failure linked to El Nino and worsening drought, they said repayment is impossible and fresh loans are unavailable. Farmers submitted petitions to the district collector and the joint registrar of cooperatives.
Article Summary: More than 100 farmers held a protest in front of the Tirupur district collectorate condemning state govt for not fully waiving cooperative crop loans. They urged govt to implement the complete waiver promised during the elections. The agitation was led by N Ramesh, Tir upur city and district secretary of Tamil Nadu Farmers Protection Association.

Article Title: Man escapes police custody in Tuticorin, caught within four hours
Article Text:
Man escapes police custody in Tuticorin, caught within four hours





Tuticorin: A 24-year-old man arrested on charges of vandalising the car of a TVK member in Tuticorin escaped from police custody on Friday morning. He was recaptured in four hours.Police said the car belonging to Rahul , 30, was parked outside his house on a street behind Our Lady of Snows Basilica. An unidentified man allegedly smashed its windows and damaged the TVK flag tied to the vehicle before fleeing.Tuticorin south police registered a case and, during the investigation, arrested Mohammed Thoufiq, 24, of Tuticorin, in connection with the incident. Around 7am on Friday, police took Thoufiq to Tuticorin Govt Medical College and Hospital for a medical examination. However, he managed to escape from police custody there. Subsequently, police launched a search and caught him around 11am.
Article Summary: Mohammed Thoufiq, 24, was arrested on charges of vandalising the car of a TVK member in Tuticorin. He was taken to a hospital for a medical examination but managed to escape. Police launched a search and caught him around 11am.

Article Title: Man moves HC seeking action against deputy speaker in attack case
Article Text:
madurai high court

Madurai:





A plea was moved by A Karthick Kumar of Trichy before Madras high court on Friday, seeking appropriate action against Tamil Nadu assembly deputy speaker and Thuraiyur TVK MLA M Ravishankar for assaulting him.Justice K Govindarajan Thilakavadi posted the matter for hearing on Dec 1 since the state sought time to get instructions.In his petition, Kumar stated that he belonged to the scheduled caste community and was involved in social activities. People of his locality have been suffering due to non-supply of drinking water for a long period. He stated that he had submitted representations to the Thuraiyur municipality and Ravishankar.He stated that on Nov 8 at about 6.30pm, while he was proceeding towards Samayapuram Temple, he noticed Ravishankar’s official vehicle parked at his residence in Manachanallur. Since he had already made representations concerning the drinking water problem affecting the residents of the locality, he decided to meet Ravishankar and bring the grievance of the public to his attention.The petitioner stated that on seeing him, Ravishankar questioned him as to who he was and where he came from.When he attempted to introduce himself, Ravishankar allegedly abused him with filthy language, brutally assaulted and threatened him. He stated that he managed to escape and went to the Manachanallur govt hospital for treatment. However, the inspector of police of Manachanallur police station compelled him to give a video statement that no assault had taken place at the residence of Ravishankar. He stated that he was threatened that a false case would be foisted against him if he did not make the video statement.Kumar stated that he had submitted a detailed representation to the Trichy district superintendent of police seeking action against the deputy speaker and the inspector. Since no action was taken, the petitioner moved court seeking relief.
Article Summary: A plea was moved by A Karthick Kumar of Trichy before Madras high court on Friday, seeking appropriate action against Tamil Nadu assembly deputy speaker. Justice K Govindarajan Thilakavadi posted the matter for hearing on Dec 1 since the state sought time to get instructions.

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Police registered a case against Sankar and arrested him. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district. He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’

Article Title: Suspected poisoning: Postmortem conducted on dog following Kerala HC intervention
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The Ernakulam district veterinary authorities, following an intervention of the high court, conducted an urgent postmortem on Friday on a dog that died under mysterious circumstances at Panangad, Kochi, to ascertain the cause of its death.The postmortem was conducted after Justice C Jayachandran directed the authorities to preserve the carcass of the dog for examination. The directive was issued on a petition filed by Jacob Thomas of Nettoor, a licensed community dog caretaker.The petitioner approached the court stating that on the morning of Nov 26, while he was out feeding community dogs along Kamala Surayya Road and Priyadarshini Road in Panangad, he found a dog in a suspected poisoned condition. Despite taking the dog to a hospital, it did not survive.Thomas further submitted that he had approached the Panangad police and Maradu municipality with petitions seeking a postmortem to ascertain the cause of death, but his requests were not entertained. He subsequently approached the HC.Senior counsel S Vinod Bhat, appearing for the petitioner, informed the court that locals were killing community dogs based on a gross misinterpretation of a Supreme Court judgment dated May 19.The petitioner had also sought a freezer facility to preserve the carcass and prevent it from decomposing.Considering the urgency of preserving the carcass, the court directed the district veterinary officer to take the necessary steps to ensure its preservation. The authorities subsequently conducted the postmortem on Friday itself.Noting that a special bench had been constituted pursuant to a Supreme Court directive to consider matters relating to stray dogs, the court also directed the registry to obtain appropriate orders from the Chief Justice and place the matter accordingly.
Article Summary: The Ernakulam district veterinary authorities conducted an urgent postmortem on a dog that died under mysterious circumstances at Panangad, Kochi. The postmortem was conducted after Justice C Jayachandran directed the authorities to preserve the carcass of the dog for examination.
